opportunities.descriptionText: The Regional Procurement Office (RPO) West, on behalf of VISN 22, hereby issues a notice of intent to pursue a non-competitive procurement with Thundercat Technology, a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), for a commercially available, FedRAMP-authorized, cloud-hosted Interactive Patient Care (IPC) ecosystem (Get Well Network). This solution will support inpatient education and engagement, digital care management, and mobile rounding for approximately four inpatient beds. It includes all required hardware, software, implementation, training, and ongoing support. The Contractor shall provide a turnkey solution, including equipment, software licenses, installation, configuration, interfaces, support services, and training necessary to deliver a fully operational system in a production environment hosted in AWS GovCloud. The intended site is Phoenix Veterans Affairs Health Care System, 650 East Indian School Road, Phoenix, AZ 85012-1839.

opportunities.descriptionText: This requirement is set aside and ONLY for the VISN1 Construction MATOC IDIQ Pool The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Veterans Integrated Service Network 1 (VISN1) anticipates awarding a VISN 1 Construction MATOC Task Order for 402-23-794 Mdernize Campus Corridors project. Project Description: The project involves a 15,600-square-foot interior renovation of the Main Street Corridor connecting Buildings B209 and B221 at the Togus VA Medical Center in Augusta, Maine. The project includes comprehensive site preparation, demolition, and construction activities to modernize the campus corridors at the Togus VA Medical Center. Work consists of replacing flooring, roofing, interior finishes, and improving HVAC systems in occupied buildings while maintaining uninterrupted medical center operations. The contractor is responsible for developing VA‑compliant phasing, life safety, security, environmental protection, and utility‑interruption plans. The effort includes strict protection of existing facilities, coordination of temporary utilities, secure document handling, adherence to safety and infection control requirements, and full restoration of affected areas. All work must be performed in accordance with the drawings, specifications, VA safety standards, and federal regulations to deliver a fully compliant, operationally safe, and modernized corridor system.
